facts.statement: Physogaleus was an extinct genus of small requiem sharks living from the Late Paleocene to the Miocene.
facts.quote: Physogaleus is an extinct genus of small requiem shark that lived from the Late Paleocene to Miocene epochs.

facts.statement: Physogaleus is known only from fossil teeth and isolated vertebrae.
facts.quote: Physogaleus is only known from fossil teeth and isolated vertebra.

facts.statement: Physogaleus teeth are smaller than true tiger shark teeth and lack the heavy serrations found in Galeocerdo.
facts.quote: Physogaleus teeth reach a maximum size that is smaller than true tiger sharks, and they lack the heavy serrations typical of Galeocerdo.

facts.statement: Physogaleus likely ate bony fish and probably grew to about 3 meters (10 feet) in length.
facts.quote: This indicates individuals of Physogaleus probably had a diet of bony fish, similar to the living sand-tiger shark, measuring 3 meters (10 ft) long.

facts.statement: The genus Physogaleus was established by Cappetta in 1980.
Physogaleus belongs to the family Carcharhinidae.
Physogaleus is classified in the class Chondrichthyes.
Physogaleus lived from the Thanetian to the Gelasian, between 59.24 and 1.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Thanetian to Gelasian (59.24 to 1.8 million years ago)

facts.statement: Physogaleus appears in the BBC book adaptation Monsters of the Sea (2003), a spin-off of Walking with Dinosaurs (1999).
facts.quote: Está presentado en la adaptación de libro de la serie de BBC Monstruos de Mar (2003), un Spin-off a Caminando entre Dinosaurios (1999).

facts.statement: In the book adaptation, Physogaleus attempts to steal a Basilosaurus kill but fails.
facts.quote: En el libro, intento robar la matanza de un Basilosaurus, sin resultados

facts.statement: Researchers created the genus Physogaleus because species within it were more morphologically similar to each other than to the genus Galeocerdo.
facts.quote: Recognition of numerous differences in dental anatomy of each of these species compared to other species of Galeocerdo lead researchers to establish the genus Physogaleus to include taxa that were more morphologically similar to one another than they were to Galeocerdo.

rejected.statement: Physogaleus teeth resemble modern tiger shark teeth but are smaller with a central cusp that projects further from the base.
rejected.quote: The teeth are similar to those of the modern Tiger shark, but are smaller, with a more central cusp that projects further from the base of the tooth.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'central cusp that projects further from the base'
